title: AI Engineer
location: North Chicago, IL, US
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. This entry-level AI Engineer will work under close supervision to apply developing technical knowledge in Software Engineering and Generative AI, performing analytic, testing, modeling, and development tasks on smaller projects, and independently on larger, more complex assignments. The role will help design, build, and deploy AI-enabled software solutions, including LLM-powered applications, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and model-serving APIs, to meet business requirements.
Responsibilities:
Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, documents methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Support development of AI-enabled applications and fix straightforward defects under close supervision.
Build and maintain components of LLM-based solutions, including API integrations, prompt and tool/function-calling workflows, and basic RAG pipelines (chunking, embeddings, vector search).
Clean, transform, and analyze data with Python, SQL, and data libraries; build simple ETL steps and visualizations.
Execute assigned test cases, including unit tests and basic retrieval or model evaluations, and help reproduce reported issues.
Serve models and AI services through RESTAPIs and containers, prepare simple configuration changes, and follow deployment runbooks.
Track experiments and model versions and support monitoring and CI/CD processes.
Document work and escalation steps in tickets and knowledge base entries.
Learn codebase, development workflows, and platform fundamentals through pairing and code reviews.
Produce reliable technical outputs, follow quality and safety standards (including AI guardrails), document reproducible methods and records, and communicate progress and risks to project leads.
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or relevant STEM certification; or 4 years of equivalent experience.
Problem decomposition, clear communication, reading documentation, collaborating through code review, and explaining results to non-technical people.
Python and Software Fundamentals Core language: data types, control flow, functions, OOP, comprehensions, generators, decorators, exceptions, file I/O, virtual environments (venv, pip / uv)
Data libraries: NumPy, pandas (cleaning, joins, groupby, time series)
Visualization: Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly
Code quality: type hints, unit testing (pytest), logging, PEP 8, packaging
APIs and web: requests, REST concepts, FastAPI or Flask to serve models, async basics
Tooling: Git/GitHub, Jupyter, VS Code, Docker basics
Databases SQL (essential): SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, indexes, query optimization
Relational databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite; schema design, normalization, primary and foreign keys, transactions
Python connectivity: SQLAlchemy, psycopg2, pandas.read_sql
NoSQL: MongoDB (documents), Redis (caching)
Vector databases (AI-specific): embeddings, similarity search, and tools such as pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Pinecone
Data pipelines: ETL basics, data warehouses, Airflow concepts
Modern GenAI Skills LLM APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, structured outputs, tool/function calling
RAG: chunking, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation
Frameworks: LangChain or LlamaIndex (know the basics, but understand what's underneath)
Agents: tool use, multi-step workflows, basic evaluation, and guardrails
MLOps and Deployment Model serving: FastAPI, Docker
Experiment tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases
Cloud basics: AWS, Azure, or GCP
CI/CD basics, monitoring, model versioning

​​Work with the business and BTS functional leads to clearly define business decisions, solution options and recommendations for a given deal based on deal model, size, complexity, risk, and speed to business value.

​Responsible for escalating cross-functional risks and issues and driving them to resolution, and driving risks and issues cross-functionally.
​​Presenting BTS updates to the function SVPs in the Executive Steering Committee.
​​Continuous improvement projects to drive speed and agility in BTS M&A services and capabilities.
Identify and implement AI innovative solutions and capabilities to challenge status quo and bring value to the business faster.

Bachelor's Degree with 9 years of experience OR Master's Degree with 8 years of experience OR PhD with 4 years of experience.
​Experience working on mergers, acquisitions, and divestiture projects across a largescale enterprise.
​​Experience leading a portfolio of business applications and leading large, complex cross-functional global IT implementations.
​​​Skilled in creating AI agents and tools to reimagine or improve a process or capability. Led and implemented multiple projects that drove speed, efficiencies, and/or cost savings.
​​Strong Project Management, Executive Stakeholder Engagement, Business Systems Applications and delivering complex cross-functional global programs.

Lead the month-end actual close process for HUMIRA, including preparation of Price, Volume/Demand, and Pipeline variance and close commentary
Present monthly actual sales results, key drivers of performance, and future-period volume forecasts to finance and commercial leadership.

Minimum of 10 years of combined experience in analytics, forecasting, and/or financial planning and analysis.

Demonstrated ability to think creatively and strategically, identify key issues, opportunities, and value drivers, and translate strategic insights into forecasts that drive business decisions.

Proven ability to design and manage multiple tasks concurrently in a dynamic environment within given timelines.

Excellent/advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills; excellent problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills

MBA / Master's in Accounting or Finance and/or CPA.
Biopharma industry experience and/or experience supporting a commercial/marketing organization.

Lead the Cross-Functional Modeling Forum (CMF): set the agenda, convene modeling practitioners from R&D, Operations, and partner functions, and establish the governance, review cycles, decision rights, and model credibility standards that keep the organization’s computational practices effective, current, and aligned with business strategy.
Lead the Computational Assisted Process Engineering (CAPE) group: directly supervise, mentor, and develop a team of modeling engineers; evaluate individual performance and own accountability for the effective performance of the team; sponsor emerging leaders, design meaningful development assignments, and recommend resource allocations.
Coordinate AI activities across the entire Small Molecule (SM) CMC organization: drive best-practice sharing and AI tool management, and guide, train, and motivate colleagues in the effective use of AI.
Set and communicate the computational process engineering strategy across drug-development programs and major capabilities, aligning technical priorities, resource recommendations, and risk decisions with program and portfolio needs.
Own the integrated computational engineering strategy from laboratory and modeling understanding through scale-up, technology transfer, and manufacturing readiness; define critical uncertainties, scale-up strategy, and manufacturing-readiness criteria, and direct the generation of data required to test key hypotheses.
Function as a principal investigator: independently conceive, execute, and communicate novel multi-disciplinary modeling and development strategies that achieve project and area goals, while contributing scientific insight to multiple other projects.
Direct the development, qualification, and deployment of multi-physics and mechanistic models – including CFD, discrete element and particle-based methods, structural, thermal, and fluid-structure interaction analysis, transport phenomena, reaction and crystallization kinetics, and reduced-order or hybrid digital twins – to address equipment design, process design space definition, scale-up, and manufacturing challenges.

Shape Process Engineering and Center of Excellence strategy through long-range capability planning, talent priorities, resource recommendations, and cross-functional operating models.

PhD with 5+ years of experience in area or scientific area of discipline. Demonstrated depth in computational engineering, with several years of applied, industrially relevant experience in multi-physics simulation and a proven record of translating simulation results into design, process, or manufacturing decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading a small team of engineers with strong modeling competence, including delegation of meaningful ownership, technical coaching, performance feedback, and accountability for team deliverables.
Proven command of engineering fundamentals – fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, solid mechanics, thermodynamics, mixing, and reaction engineering – combined with the numerical methods, meshing, solver, and convergence judgment required to produce trustworthy results.

Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to translate complex computational concepts into clear, actionable recommendations for technical experts, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership.

Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another regulated industry, including exposure to GxP compliance, technology transfer, and CMC regulatory content.
Experience applying computational methods to pharmaceutical unit operations such as mixing and blending, crystallization, filtration and drying, lyophilization, granulation, tableting, spray drying, sterile and aseptic processing, single-use systems, or fill-finish.
Experience with discrete element modeling (DEM), population balance modeling, multiphase and free-surface flows, non-Newtonian rheology, and coupled CFD-DEM or fluid-structure interaction approaches.

Lead electrical and electronic design activities for battery-powered electromechanical medical devices and drug-delivery systems.

title: Policy Lead, California
location: California, United States
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's US & Canada Public Policy team represents Airbnb and the interests of our community of hosts and guests before the legislators, regulators, opinion leaders and coalitions who shape the political and legal environment for our business. We operate in heavily regulated spaces in the technology sector: short-term rental rules are written and rewritten at the state, county and municipal level, and the outcomes directly determine where and how Airbnb can grow.
The Difference You Will Make:
The Policy Lead, California holds ultimate responsibility for Airbnb's public policy and regulatory strategy in the state. This is a senior leadership position accountable for three interlocking outcomes:
Business growth. Protecting and expanding Airbnb's ability to operate across California by securing workable regulatory frameworks at the state and local level and defending against measures that would restrict supply or impose restrictive compliance burdens.
Regulatory affairs. Managing an active, high-volume docket of state legislation, local ordinances, administrative rulemaking and enforcement,  ensuring Airbnb's position is well represented in each.
Brand reputation among policymakers. Above all, materially improving how lawmakers, regulators and civic leaders perceive Airbnb and its host community, and converting that credibility into durable policy outcomes.
The role is as much internal as it is external. You will  lead a team of Policy Managers covering California's priority markets, manage a bench of external consultants and lobbyists, and be accountable for the state's annual policy budget. Equally important, the Lead serves as the central point of alignment between Public Policy and the cross-functional partners whose decisions shape our regulatory position: Legal, Supply, Communications, Marketing, Safety, Tax, and the business leadership for the region. title: Sr. Regulatory Technical program Manager, Direct-to-Device (D2D), Amazon Leo, Regulatory, Authorization Readiness & Compliance (ARC)
location: Arlington, Virginia, USA
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's initiative to launch a constellation of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to provide affordable, reliable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Direct-to-Device (D2D) is a groundbreaking service that will bring satellite connectivity directly to everyday mobile devices, extending coverage beyond the reach of traditional terrestrial networks. To enable this, the Regulatory team obtains licenses and approvals for space, services, ground-based infrastructure, and the spectrum required to serve customers in each country where Amazon Leo will operate. There is no globally unified regulatory licensing regime for a LEO system like Amazon Leo, and most countries lack established D2D licensing frameworks entirely.
We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to join the Authorization Readiness and Compliance (ARC) team, a sub-function within the Regulatory organization at Amazon Leo. You will own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading implementation of the D2D-specific authorization plans defined by Regulatory Licensing Leads across priority countries. You will work directly with regional Regulatory TPMs, Legal, and Regulatory Licensing Leads to drive execution across FCC, ITU, and country regulators in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions, ensuring Amazon Leo can offer commercial D2D service on day one in every priority country.
D2D is a first-of-its-kind satellite service category. ITU rules continue to evolve, and jurisdictions impose conflicting spectrum and interference requirements. You will navigate that uncertainty, exercising independent judgment to implement the authorization readiness path forward where no clear precedent exists. This role demands technical fluency in Radio Frequency (RF) spectrum allocations, interference analysis, satellite communications, and 3GPP Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) standards. You will lead the implementation of complex license conditions and, in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, translate obligations into precise engineering requirements that software and operations teams can act on. You will also design and build a licensing obligation tracking platform and automated compliance reporting pipeline to manage thousands of license conditions at scale.
Key job responsibilities
•Own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading the implementation of the authorization path, tracking milestones, and driving resolution of blockers across priority countries.
•Interpret complex license conditions across FCC, ITU, and country-level regulators, and in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, convert obligations into actionable engineering requirements for software and operations teams.
•Drive cross-functional coordination with engineering, infrastructure, business, and operations teams to align authorization timelines with service launch schedules.
•Influence without authority across senior stakeholders in matrixed organizations, resolving competing priorities between customer commitments, engineering constraints, and regulatory realities.
•Identify and escalate regulatory risks with clear mitigation strategies to maintain compliance and prevent operational disruptions.
•Provide senior leadership visibility on D2D authorization readiness, launch risk, and country-by-country compliance status.
•Own the regulatory stakeholder relationship with key customers and partners, delivering precise updates on D2D authorization status and maintaining trust through consistent follow-through.
•Set a course in the face of ambiguity to deliver independently, asking the right questions, clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately.
Export Control
This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.
A day in the life
You will serve as the critical link between the Regulatory team and the broader Amazon Leo organization, driving cross-functional priorities with engineering, infrastructure, and business teams, and providing senior leadership visibility into D2D authorization readiness and launch risk. A key part of this role is managing the regulatory relationship with customer and partner stakeholders who maintain high expectations for communication precision, timeline accuracy, and compliance rigor. You will translate complex, evolving regulatory positions into clear narratives, set and manage expectations across competing priorities, and maintain trust through disciplined follow-through. The right candidate will have successfully managed multi-discipline telecommunications program initiatives, possess a well-rounded technical background in satellite communications, and demonstrate excellent verbal and written communication skills.
About the team
The Regulatory team secures and safeguards Amazon Leo's access to radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbital resources around the world, addresses ground infrastructure licensing and regulatory requirements, and shapes the policies and regulatory requirements that affect our ability to deliver on business goals, enabling delivery of broadband and D2D services to Amazon Leo's customers. The organization operates through three sub-functions: (i) Shaping Policy: leads public consultations, advocacy, and rulemakings at national, regional, and international levels to secure country entry, improve licensing frameworks, enable spectrum access, and prevent undesirable compliance requirements on Amazon Leo; (ii) Securing Authorizations: obtains the licenses required across broadband and D2D services and engages regulators to resolve licensing barriers and secure spectrum access and use rights; and (iii) Executing on Obligations: establishes Lawful Intercept (LI) and Law Enforcement Response (LER) programs by jurisdiction, fulfills the spectrum and network related obligations attached to held authorizations, and demonstrates compliance with service obligations. These obligations range from absolute (e.g., LI/LER) to defensible (e.g., certifications, reporting, fees, content blocking, regulator engagement), where failure carries fines, license revocations, service disruptions, and reputational damage.
The team partners with Business, Legal, Public Policy, and Public Relations to execute the strategy, and align with Design, Engineering, Operations, Security, and Business teams to keep the Plan of Record (POR) synchronized with regulatory requirements.

title: Deployment Operations Associate
location: Bloomingdale, IL
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is looking for an Operations Associate to support our Chicagoland team from our Bloomingdale, IL warehouse.

This is a foundational hire for Base's expansion across the Chicagoland area.  The ideal candidate is organized, comfortable navigating local building & permitting offices, and treats a stack of paperwork like a checklist to clear, not an obstacle.

You'll be the person who accelerates our expansion: partnering with municipal offices across Chicagoland to keep our install pipeline moving, while also keeping our Bloomingdale office and warehouse running day to day. The ideal candidate is organized, comfortable navigating local bureaucracy, and treats a stack of paperwork like a checklist to clear, not an obstacle.



What You'll Do

 - Permitting: Prints permits and inspection packages and stages them in a clean, labeled permitting area, so crews can pick up their packet and go the next morning.

 - In-person permitting (small, repeatable trips): picks up and pays for permits at AHJs as they become ready, two to three afternoons a week, rotating by area (West, Southwest, North). Works from the Bloomingdale warehouse in the mornings, using a company card for fees and mileage reimbursement for travel. Scans, emails, and files each permit the same or next day.

 - Inspections: backup contact for inspectors on inspection day. Confirms timing changes and makes sure an electrician is on site. Right now last minute changes are routing through electricians who might be unavailable.

 - Placards and labels: learn to run the engraver so we can make a placard the same day an inspection needs one, instead of waiting on a shipment.

 - Office: acts as office manager. Keeps supplies, the kitchen, and snacks stocked, greets visitors, and keeps the office well cared for, so the crew and warehouse staff have what they need.

 - As things come up: picks up quick-turn tasks that unblock installs and inspections, such as supply runs, last-minute printing, or documents an AHJ needs.

 - Works with: onsite staff, the permitting team at HQ, and Workplace and IT to make sure the office has everything we need.



What You'll Bring

 - 1–3 years of administrative or office coordination experience

 - Comfort with in-person, paperwork-heavy processes and a track record of following through on multi-step tasks

 - A valid driver's license (a company vehicle is provided for AHJ visits)

 - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.  This role tracks a lot of moving pieces across multiple jurisdictions

 - Spanish fluency is a plus, not required
   
   

About this Team

Base's Field Operations team is the tactical engine behind getting batteries installed in Chicago-area homes. As Base scales across Illinois, permitting is one of the biggest bottlenecks.  Some AHJs still require someone to physically show up to register, file, or pay before an install can even be scheduled. This role sits at the center of that work, in an in-person, paperwork-driven side of grid modernization that's just as critical as the installs themselves. You'll report to Base's Chicago Deployments Engineer and work closely with the electricians, crew leads, and AHJ-relations team opening up new jurisdictions across Chicagoland.





Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

title: Manufacturing Engineer
location: Weirton, WV
description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

We are looking for a Manufacturing/Process Engineer to join our Cathode Advanced Manufacturing Engineering Team. This role will focus on commissioning new product lines, developing robust process specifications and collaborating with equipment and operations teams to optimize efficiency, quality, and scalability. This role will focus on calendering and roll to roll web handling across equipment centers. Beyond supporting our newly operational manufacturing line, this role will contribute to the development of next-generation manufacturing processes as we expand production capabilities.



Your experience and creativity will enable you to create and implement world class, fully automated processes that enable the production of our first-of-a kind grid storage technology. This is an exciting opportunity to develop processes from scratch and have a large impact on the future of our manufacturing while doing your part to help combat climate change. Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Commission and qualify processes in a fast-paced manufacturing environment with tight timelines. You will lead the commissioning of calendering equipment and support your fellow engineers in troubleshooting, designing and commissioning web handling portions of their scopes.

 - Perform equipment and process capability studies while documenting and continuously improving the process steps that deliver Form’s Air cathode.

 - Work closely with equipment and operations teams to identify process bottlenecks and implement solutions both on existing equipment and for following equipment iterations

 - Independently drive projects for line upgrades on existing equipment

 - Contribute to the development of new manufacturing processes for future production phases.

 - Document process changes, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and best practices.

 - Be a champion for safety while scaling initial process designs to full production volume.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Chemical, Industrial, or related field).

 - 1–3 years of experience in process engineering, manufacturing, or continuous improvement roles.

 - Strong problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to process optimization.

 - Experience with process development, statistical analysis, and root cause problem-solving techniques.

 - Proficiency with statistical methods and tools (JMP, Minitab, or equivalent) is preferred.

 - Ability to work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and maintenance teams.

 - Hands-on experience with manufacturing equipment and process troubleshooting is a plus.

 - Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other process improvement methodologies is beneficial.
   




WHERE YOU'LL WORK:



This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. Relocation assistance is available.



 #LI-Onsite

 #LI-JM2



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.




If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will never solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.

location: Deerfield, ILLINOIS, US
description:
Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.
We are building a company that is determined to win, and we are clear about how: strong brands, great people, and disciplined execution.
You'll join a team that puts customers first, keeps its commitments, and cuts through complexity to deliver meaningful results.
If you're looking for an opportunity to make an impact and help shape what's next for our iconic brands, we'd love to meet you. Apply now.
Explore life at Fortune Brands here .
The Director, Finance – Global Sourcing serves as the strategic finance leader supporting Fortune Brands Innovations' Global Sourcing organization and holds financial ownership for indirect procurement activities. Reporting to the Sr Director, Operations Finance , this role is the primary finance business partner to the VP, Global Sourcing and their leadership team, providing financial leadership, strategic decision support, and insight across a global direct material spend portfolio exceeding $2 billion annually, while leading the governance, strategy, and value delivery agenda for indirect spend.
This role is responsible for leading the financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and value realization processes supporting global sourcing initiatives, including commodity inflation and deflation management, purchase price variance, supplier negotiations, continuous improvement savings, working capital optimization, and standard costing activities.. The Director will proactively influence direct and indirect sourcing and procurement strategy through rigorous financial analysis, fact-based recommendations, and cross-functional partnership across Operations, Supply Chain, FP&A, Business Unit Finance, and corporate functions.
The role manages a team of two Financial Analysts and is expected to drive both talent development and continuous improvement across Global Sourcing Finance processes.
Position Location: Hybrid (Deerfield, IL) – 3 days per week in office. (Flexibility to work from home Mondays and Fridays)
RESPONSIBLIITIES:
Strategic Finance Partnership
Serve as the lead finance partner to the Global Sourcing leadership team, providing financial guidance and strategic decision support across sourcing initiatives and priorities.
Develop trusted advisor relationships with sourcing leaders by providing objective, data-driven insights and constructive challenge to business assumptions.
Support the development and execution of sourcing strategies that improve profitability, cost competitiveness, cash flow, and enterprise value creation.
Translate complex sourcing and market dynamics into actionable recommendations for Operations, Finance, and Executive Leadership.
Financial Planning, Forecasting & Reporting
Lead forecasting, annual planning, and long-range planning processes related to direct material spend, inflation/deflation, purchase price variance (PPV), supplier rebates, and sourcing productivity initiatives.
Establish and maintain financial models used to forecast commodity, currency, and supplier cost impacts across the enterprise.
Provide financial oversight and guidance for standard cost development and annual costing processes.
Direct monthly reporting and communication of sourcing-related financial performance, key risks, opportunities, and variance analysis.
Ensure alignment between sourcing forecasts, Operations Finance, FP&A, and Business Unit financial commitments.
Commodity, Supplier & Cost Management
Lead financial analysis of commodity and currency market trends to identify risks, opportunities, and actionable sourcing recommendations.
Provide financial leadership and support during supplier negotiations, contract development, and cost management initiatives.
Oversee purchase price variance analysis and value-realization tracking to ensure sourcing initiatives deliver expected results.
Direct financial evaluation of inflation mitigation, supplier productivity, and continuous improvement initiatives across the sourcing portfolio.
Lead financial assessment of supplier concentration, continuity, country, tariff, duty, currency, and geopolitical risks, including scenario modeling and mitigation recommendations.
Evaluate total landed cost and total cost of ownership when supporting supplier selection, sourcing transitions, localization, dual-sourcing, and make-versus-buy decisions.
Working Capital & Value Creation
Partner with sourcing leadership to improve working capital performance through supplier payment term optimization and cash flow improvement initiatives.
Monitor and communicate the financial impact of sourcing-related working capital initiatives and contractual changes.
Validate realized savings and identify risks to value achievement, ensuring financial commitments are accurately measured and reported.
Establish a consistent performance-management framework and executive scorecard for sourcing productivity, cost avoidance, purchase price variance, inflation and deflation, rebates, payment terms, working capital, forecast accuracy, and value realization.
Define common baselines, ownership, timing, and validation standards so that sourcing benefits are measured consistently and reconciled to reported financial results.
Team Leadership & Process Improvement
Lead, coach, and develop a team of two Senior Financial Analysts, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Establish priorities, allocate resources, and ensure effective execution of team responsibilities.
Build organizational capability through mentoring, succession planning, performance management, and development planning.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance reporting, forecasting accuracy, financial insights, automation, and overall process efficiency.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate closely with Operations Finance, Supply Chain, FP&A, Business Unit Finance, Procurement, and Operations leaders to ensure financial alignment and consistent methodologies.
Influence business decisions across functions without formal authority through strong relationships, credibility, and analytical rigor.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or related field.
7+ years of progressive finance experience required; 10+ years preferred.
Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including coaching, development, and performance management.
Experience supporting sourcing, procurement, supply chain, operations, manufacturing, or related functions.
Demonstrated success leading financial planning, forecasting, business analysis, and strategic decision support activities.
Strong analytical and financial modeling capabilities with the ability to evaluate complex business scenarios.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and effectively challenge assumptions through fact-based recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complex financial concepts into clear business insights.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and financial reporting tools.
Experience with financial systems such as Oracle, SAP, BPC, HFM, Essbase, Tableau, or similar platforms.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required to support sourcing priorities, supplier engagements, and team collaboration.
Preferred Qualifications
MBA, CPA, CMA, or other advanced business or finance credential.
Strong knowledge of procurement finance concepts, including total cost of ownership, total landed cost, purchase price variance, commodity and foreign-exchange exposure, supplier rebates, payment terms, and sourcing savings validation.
Experience working within multinational manufacturing or consumer products environments.
Experience developing commodity, currency, or supplier cost forecasting models.
Proven track record of leading process improvement and finance transformation initiatives.

title: Bid Desk Analyst

description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
The Bid Desk Analyst supports the commercial and sales organization by coordinating and analyzing customer bid and quotation activities. This role serves as a central resource for managing requests for quotation (RFQs), gathering required information, analyzing pricing and cost data, and ensuring accurate, timely, and competitive bid submissions.
The Bid Desk Analyst works cross-functionally with Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and other stakeholders to develop complete and commercially sound proposals. The position requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, organization, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
· Coordinate and manage the bid and quotation process from initial request through submission.
· Review customer RFQs, bid requirements, specifications, and supporting documentation to identify requirements, deadlines, and potential risks.
· Gather and consolidate pricing, cost, lead time, product, freight, and other information required to prepare customer quotations.
· Analyze historical pricing, cost information, market data, and other relevant information to support pricing recommendations.
· Prepare accurate and competitive quotes in accordance with established pricing strategies, guidelines, and approval requirements.
· Partner with Sales and other internal stakeholders to clarify customer requirements and ensure bid responses are complete and accurate.
· Coordinate with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance to obtain technical, operational, and financial inputs.
· Identify gaps, inconsistencies, or risks within bid requirements and escalate issues as appropriate.
· Maintain accurate bid documentation, pricing files, assumptions, and supporting information.
· Track open bids and quotation activity, including status, deadlines, submissions, and outcomes.
· Support analysis of bid win/loss results and identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement.
· Develop and maintain reports and dashboards related to bid activity, pricing, pipeline, and performance metrics.
· Assist with continuous improvement of bid desk processes, tools, templates, and workflows.
· Ensure pricing and quote information is handled confidentially and in accordance with company policies and controls.
· Provide timely follow-up and communication to ensure bids are completed and submitted within customer deadlines.
· Support strategic contract and bid opportunity assessment by analyzing customer buying patterns, renewal opportunities, competitive positioning, whitespace opportunities, historical performance, and profitability trends to inform bid strategy and commercial decision-making
· Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
· This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Education and Work Experience
· Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Supply Chain, Marketing, or a related field or equivalent relevant work experience.
· 2+ years of relevant experience in quoting, pricing, sales operations, business analysis, customer service, supply chain, or a related field.
· Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
· Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
· Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously.
· Strong written and verbal communication skills.
· Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
· Ability to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
Desired Education/Experience
· Experience working with RFQs, bids, proposals, or commercial pricing.
· Experience with ERP, CRM, CPQ, or other pricing/quotation systems.
· Experience analyzing pricing, margins, costs, and competitive information.
· Experience with Power BI or other data visualization/reporting tools.
Certificates and Licenses
No specific certificates or licenses are preferred or required.
Job —Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
· Bid, RFQ, and quotation processes
· Pricing, costing, margins, and commercial practices
· Customer and sales support processes
· Data analysis and reporting
· ERP/CRM/CPQ systems and Microsoft Excel
· Cross-functional business processes and internal controls
· Excellent MS Office (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word) capabilities required
COMPETENCIES
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies.
· Analytical Thinking: Uses data and sound judgment to evaluate information, identify trends, and support business decisions.
· Attention to Detail: Ensures accuracy and completeness of pricing, quotes, documentation, and customer requirements.
· Business Acumen: Understands the relationship between pricing, cost, margin, customer requirements, and business objectives.
· Collaboration: Builds effective working relationships across Sales, Operations, Finance, and other functions.
· Customer Focus: Understands customer needs and ensures bid responses are accurate, timely, and responsive.
· Organization & Prioritization: Effectively manages multiple bids, deadlines, and competing priorities.
· Communication: Clearly communicates requirements, assumptions, risks, and recommendations to internal stakeholders.
· Continuous Improvement: Identifies opportunities to improve the efficiency, consistency, and effectiveness of the bid process.
· Pricing & Commercial Analysis: Assesses pricing scenarios, profitability impacts, contract terms, and commercial risks to support competitive and financially sound proposals.

· Project Management: Effectively coordinates multiple bids, stakeholders, deliverables, approvals, and deadlines while maintaining quality and responsiveness.

· Adaptability: Responds effectively to changing priorities, customer demands, and business requirements in a fast-paced environment.

description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Company Description
At Intuitive, we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints. Our innovations in robotic-assisted surgery and diagnostics, digital ecosystems, and integrated service solutions are transforming how healthcare is delivered.
To support the next phase of company growth, the Program Management Office (PMO) is establishing a new Global Expansion  team focused on accelerating access to our existing, commercially available da Vinci and ION technologies in underpenetrated price-sensitive procedures, countries and sites of care.  This requires close partnership with commercial leadership, business units and shared services to ensure strategic priorities are translated into scalable business outcomes and global product launches are executed with agility and confidence.
Primary Function of Position
The Director, Global Expansion, is responsible for establishing this new vertical within the PMO, ensuring robust project management execution to scale global commercialization of existing da Vinci and ION technologies in underpenetrated price-sensitive procedures, countries and sites of care, in line with the aggressive roadmaps and targets that are being established.
This role will partner with Commercial leaders, Product Management, Engineering, Regulatory, Finance, Quality, Supply Chain, and Marketing to execute the 3-year roadmap for regional expansion, remove barriers, and align cross-functional resources to deliver committed launch (APL) timelines for various regions as prioritized by commercial leadership. Success is defined by the ability to build a high-performing team which converts long-range roadmap strategies into coordinated and executable plans that accelerate market expansion, customer adoption, and business growth.
Essential Job Duties
Product Introduction Planning & Readiness Execution
For products that are already commercially available, the PMO Director will:
Work closely with the Regional Leads who define the product launch roadmap into each country and lead the PMO GMA team to create detailed plans to support regional launches.
Ensure plans cover the necessary scope of activity required to achieve APL / launch readiness, with the necessary timelines and resources.
Assess cross-functional resource capacity and constraints needed to support regional launch roadmap. Escalate resource gaps and/or trade offs required to support successful execution
Ensure project risks and constraints are recognized, and mitigation plans are evaluated and carried out.
Manage the PMO GMA team along with cross-functional resources to execute project plans, monitoring progress and removing barriers to their success where necessary.
Provide portfolio inputs and insights to the Regional Leads so they can evaluate roadmap adjustments where necessary and agree to the final plan.
Support a periodic (quarterly) review of progress / launch readiness, new incoming requests, priorities and risks to help the Regional Leads balance their own market entry plans, priorities and expectations so that they can maintain realistic product launch roadmaps for each country.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
To support the acceleration of launch (APL) Readiness, the PMO GMA Director will:
Build effective working relationships and collaborate with a range of partners and stakeholders across the business, establishing trusted partnerships at all levels of the organization to accelerate execution, and strengthen cross-functional alignment on shared goals and timelines.
Serve as a delivery partner to Commercial, Sales and Marketing leadership, ensuring launch plans are aligned with commercial readiness, operational readiness and global/regional priorities for market entry.
Communicate timely and clearly so that the holistic portfolio view is understood, along with progress on APL / Launch readiness, and any risks, constraints or priority conflicts.
Specifically:
Business Units - multi-year plans to support product roadmaps.
PMO BU Teams - delivery of specific product changes that may be required to achieve a new market entry.
Regional and Country Marketing - commercial launch planning, and field readiness.
Commercial Leadership (Market GMs and Regional VP) - market readiness, and commercial priorities.
Finance – provide necessary updates to ensure the Finance team can maintain financial models / reporting and support the regional teams as necessary.
Regulatory Affairs (Regional and Country) - Filing and approval timelines.
Manufacturing, Master Scheduling & Supply Chain - Production forecasts, inventory positioning, supply readiness.
Tech Pubs - IFU development, labeling, and translations aligned to regional launch timelines.
Service – business systems readiness, training, field replaceable units (FRU) inventory
Team Leadership
Build a new vertical within the PMO organization, focused on the acceleration of commercially available products into new markets. Hire and develop talent to build a capable and resilient team that can operate in a highly matrixed area of the business.
Ensure all team members excel in project management and use the best practice 9-step project management approach that has been developed by the PMO.
Develop a culture of accountability and operational excellence that reliably delivers launches on time.
Process Improvement and Best Practice
To help accelerate market entry projects for commercially available products, the PMO GMA Director will:
Build on the work already done to capture the launch readiness checklists and associated activities, by adding more specific details and documenting tribal knowledge, turning it into repeatable processes that can be used by all team members.
Identify and deploy best practices from a variety of sources to continuously enhance overall business launch capability and deliver value to the regional hubs.
Identify systemic barriers to execution and implement sustainable solutions that improve productivity, and cross-functional collaboration at scale.
Leverage Clarity PPM tool and identify and implement other standard tools to help scale up resource capability and enhance project delivery.
Establish metrics and performance indicators to measure process effectiveness and readiness of the planned launches.
Reduce time to market of new launches by reinforcing a culture of exploration and enquiry within the team to drive continuous improvement.
Required Skills and Experience
10+ years of experience in program management, business operations, strategy, or PMO leadership in medical device industry or highly regulated industry.
Proven experience leading large-scale, cross-functional programs in complex global organizations.
Strong executive presence with the ability to influence and align senior stakeholders.

The Incubator within Future Forward at Intuitive is a cross-functional innovation group focused on identifying, evaluating, and developing new clinical opportunities and technology platforms. The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.

Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.

MD or DO required; active clinical practice is valued but not required for candidates with substantial innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Must demonstrate at least one of the following experience profiles: (1) meaningful hands-on clinical practice or procedural care experience plus exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) strong venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, corporate strategy, or product strategy experience plus sufficient clinical fluency to evaluate medical needs and care pathways.
Ability to identify unmet clinical needs and convert observations into structured hypotheses, need statements, development plans, or investment theses.
Experience conducting clinician, patient, or stakeholder interviews and synthesizing voice-of-customer input into actionable product or strategy recommendations.
Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where the path forward is uncertain and evidence must be built iteratively.
Strong cross-functional influence skills and ability to collaborate with engineering, clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, product, and business stakeholders.

MD or DO required.

Clinical practice experience, residency/fellowship training, or comparable patient-care exposure preferred for candidates coming from a primarily clinical background.

title: National Account Manager C&U
location: United States of America
description:
Plan and execute the activities of promotion and sales in multiple areas in a given region. Generate, plan, and follow up daily and monthly sales targets and actuals to achieve the sales targets of the region. Support and approve initiation, expenditures, and implementation of investments to meet the company's business requirements. Work in close cooperation with sales force effectiveness and market research professionals to effectively utilize the sales representatives and look for training opportunities and assignments that would enable their personal and career development. Follow up and increase the performance of each sales representative in the region by making double visits and carrying out periodical coaching. This is a first level of sales management.
Job Purpose
​​As a National Account Manager, you will be responsible for a specified channel. This role is uniquely positioned for an ambitious leader who is craving full ownership and accountability for our products and customers within the assigned Accounts. This is not a traditional sales role. We are searching for a candidate who shows a high level of ownership for their business and is adept at selling solutions and has a proven ability to win new business. We are seeking a candidate who is eager to be a leader, influencer and activator with internal and external key stakeholders from the first day on the job. ​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Serve as a key liaison between Kraft Heinz, the Sales organization, and assigned customers and partners, building strong relationships that drive profitable growth within the Non-Commercial Foodservice segment.
Develop and lead channel-specific priorities across K-12, College & University (C&U), Business & Industry (B&I), and Healthcare to deliver quarterly and annual growth goals, increase market penetration, and grow market share.
Manage and develop relationships across GPO/CMC partners, including Foodbuy/Compass, Entegra/Sodexo, Aramark/Avendra, Premier, and Vizient, while identifying opportunities to establish new Non-Commercial partnerships.
Serve as a subject matter expert within the Non-Commercial segment, using market, customer, insights, and sales data to identify opportunities, analyze performance gaps, target potential customers, and develop data-driven growth strategies.
Develop, track, analyze, and evaluate customer and channel business plans based on Kraft Heinz priorities, customer strategies, and external market factors to drive total customer profitability.
Lead Joint Business Planning with strategic and small-to-mid-tier accounts, tailoring programs to customer strategies while aligning with Kraft Heinz business objectives.
Build and manage a profitable sales pipeline, driving conversion of opportunities and identifying incremental branded opportunities with new and existing customers.
Grow assigned customer business through achievement of revenue and profitability targets, share gains, new and core item distribution, and effective management of Customer P&L and EBITDA objectives.
Develop customer selling stories and recommendations using insights, analytics, and market data to support business opportunities and influence customer decisions.
Develop and track Non-Commercial KPIs and sales metrics, regularly communicating wins, performance gaps, pipeline progress, and areas of opportunity during key sales meetings and business reviews.
Prepare and present periodic customer business reviews, effectively communicating business performance, opportunities, recommendations, and forward-looking strategies.
Lead and support contract negotiations, deal creation, customer presentations, and other commercial discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
Guide trade-spend strategy by channel, evaluate program ROI, and recommend or negotiate adjustments to maximize the effectiveness and profitability of trade investments.
Partner cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Legal, Culinary, Marketing, R&D, and other key stakeholders to develop customer programs, new SKUs, sales collateral, and solutions that support execution of business plans.
Support S&OP and forecasting processes, including demand planning and waste-mitigation efforts.
Challenge internal and external teams to think creatively, develop new solutions, and capitalize on emerging business opportunities.
Demonstrate strong financial and analytical acumen, including the ability to build business cases, evaluate ROI, interpret sales performance, and influence P&L outcomes.
Operate with an entrepreneurial, action-oriented mindset, demonstrating ownership, sound decision-making, perseverance, and the ability to solve complex business problems.
Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication, presentation, influence, and negotiation skills across both internal and external stakeholders.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, sales, or related field preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
​Prior sales experience required with a demonstration of major account management resulting in profitable volume, customer penetration, attainment of new business and growth.
​Experience in national accounts sales, restaurant, culinary, and/or distributor industry preferred. Experience within the Education (K-12, Colleges, University) channel preferred.
​Command of business acumen and strong business intuition demonstrated by discernment that not every sales opportunity is equal and a track record of securing profitable volume and walking away from less profitable deals.
​Strong analytical skills demonstrated by previous experience utilizing systems for tracking and recording sales, effective business planning and data-driven strategy for maintaining current and securing new customers.
​Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, demonstrated by effective presentation, influence, and advanced negotiation skills with both internal and external stakeholders.
​Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
​Must have a valid driver’s license and meet MVR requirements.
​Overnight Travel is required, and the amount varies by territory.​

Changing the World, One Kibble at a Time
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for an Associate Relations (AR) Manager to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food crafter with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. From our humble beginnings, founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry. Our purpose,  To Earn Pet Lover Trust Every Day so Pets Thrive for a Lifetime ,  provides the foundation for our highest aspirations as a company.
Being a partner to the communities that surround us – and the environment that sustains us – are top priorities.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here’s the scoop - Summary
This is an exciting opportunity for a growing HR professional to make a significant contribution to the success of a highly respected global brand by supporting the organization's ability to foster a positive, respectful, and compliant workplace.
The Associate Relations (AR) Manager will be the point of contact for Associate Relations issues and inquiries within cross-functional client groups in corporate and manufacturing teams in Canada and the US. Responsibilities include building trust, credibility, and collaborative relationships with line managers and Associates.
In this role, the AR Manager will apply expertise and sound judgement when managing inquiries, mitigating risk and minimizing adverse impact on the organization by applying policies and practices and adhering to legal and regulatory requirements.
The AR Manager will resolve issues and address client needs to ensure situations are resolved fairly, objectively, and in a manner that aligns with our Champion Values, Mars Five Principles, and the Associate Concept.
The AR Manager will report to the Sr Director, Global P&O COEs & Operations and work out of our Corporate office in either Edmonton, AB, Louisville, CO or Nashville, TN on a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person.
This role will also travel occasionally to our Kitchen in Auburn, KY. The successful candidate will build strong relationships across the organization while supporting fair, consistent, and proactive Associate Relations practices.
What a typical day looks like
Conduct timely, thorough, and effective investigations relating to company policy, employment law, and other regulations.
Support the intake, tracking, and administration of Associate Relations cases, ensuring accurate, timely, and confidential documentation.
Serve as a key contact for Associates and Leaders regarding Associate Relations questions, providing guidance on policies, processes, available resources, and policy interpretation.

Ensure proper case documentation is maintained to support compliance requirements and minimize organizational risk.
Escalate complex, sensitive, or high-risk Associate Relations matters to the appropriate partners for review and resolution.

Analyze case data, exit interview feedback, and workplace trends to identify emerging risks and opportunities for proactive action, and prepare reports, dashboards, and insights to support decision-making and Associate Relations strategies.
Support Associate experience initiatives by coordinating exit interviews, stay interviews, culture pulse activities, and other feedback-gathering mechanisms.
Support the development and continuous improvement of Associate Relations processes, tools, policies, and case management practices.
Assist with transformation initiatives, change management activities, severance agreement coordination, and other special projects as required.

5+ years of experience working in Human Resources, Employee Relations, & Employment Law preferred
Strong data and analytical skills inclusive of Excel, PowerPoint and Microsoft Co-pilot
Strong communication, written and interpersonal skills; ability to work and communicate effectively with a wide range of individuals across all levels of the organization
Ability to rapidly mobilize and manage internal and external resources to mitigate risks to the Mars business and reputation
Ability to handle and maintain confidential and sensitive information
Previous experience in CPG/Manufacturing strongly preferred
Strong conflict management skills
Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment
Strong stakeholder management
Ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, and work effectively while managing competing projects and/or demanding clients.
Motivated, energetic, goal-oriented, with a strong work ethic and positive team attitude.
A well-defined sense of diplomacy, including solid negotiation, conflict resolution, and people management skills.
Demonstrating cultural adaptability and flexing work hours given the geographical spread of responsibility.

Industry Competitive Benefits:  Medical, dental, vision and employee assistance programs to meet your individual or family needs.
Continuing Education:  In house & online learning & development, as well as an education assistance program.
Quality:  a dedication to uphold the highest standards of authenticity, nutritional integrity, and food safety, to earn the trust of Pet Lovers everywhere.

description:
Job Description:
Job: Logistics Lead
Shift: Night Shift (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM)
Location: Mars Petcare (North Kansas City, MO)
Position Type: Full-Time, Distribution & Transportation Operations
About Mars Petcare
Mars Petcare is proud to actively recruit, develop, and promote transitioning military service members and veterans. Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity—the chance to leverage the leadership, operational discipline, and mission focus gained during your military career to direct world-class supply chains that produce beloved global pet care brands like Greenies.
At Mars, you will work with real purpose, supported by talented, diverse peers guided by The Five Principles: Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom. We provide the tools, ongoing learning through our in-house Mars University, and professional mobility needed to turn your military service into a rewarding long-term civilian career.
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced Logistics Lead for our overnight operations (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM) in North Kansas City, MO. In this specialized individual contributor and frontline leadership role, you will oversee day-to-day distribution and transportation activities, coordinate with freight carriers and third-party logistics (3PL) partners, manage transactional inventory data systems, and ensure seamless throughput across our evening operating window.
This position is ideally suited for transitioning military non-commissioned officers (NCOs), petty officers, warrant officers, or logistics officers with proven experience leading personnel, managing assets under tight timelines, and directing transportation movements.
What Are We Looking For? (Requirements)
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent level of verified military/professional experience.
Relevant Experience: 3 to 6 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, distribution, or transportation operations, demonstrating the judgment to handle unexpected operational hurdles and advise cross-functional teammates.
Leadership & Supervision: Proven background supervising and directing personnel, equipment, and resources to achieve mission-critical goals under tight deadlines.
Coordination Experience: Demonstrated track record (at least 4 to 6 months) of planning, organizing, and orchestrating the daily work assignments of team members.
Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to brief operational status, communicate clearly with external carriers, and maintain shift accountability.
Partnership & Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build strong partnerships and collaborate across production, warehousing, and carrier networks to achieve shared performance targets.
Shift Availability: Dedicated availability to work the overnight schedule (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM).
Key Responsibilities
Transportation & Distribution Operations:
Provide operational oversight for overnight distribution workflows, serving as the first-line leader for transactional operations in shipping, receiving, and staging.
Coordinate activities of third-party carriers, subcontractors, and freight vendors, serving as their primary operational point of contact during the night shift under an established contract management framework.
Ensure all distribution operations comply with safety standards, quality control protocols, and Mars operating procedures.
Systems & Data Management:
Utilize enterprise warehouse and transportation data management systems (WMS/TMS) to access real-time shipping data, track order fulfillment, reconcile manifests, and manage bill of lading (BOL) documentation.
Monitor performance indicators (KPIs) to spot movement bottlenecks and execute proactive recovery plans.
Stakeholder & Supplier Coordination:
Maintain strong relationships with external logistics providers and internal plant teams, resolving operational escalations and ensuring on-time delivery schedules.
Support client- and vendor-facing communication, handling inquiries with clarity and professionalism.
Team Leadership & Development:
Supervise, coach, and mentor night shift operational associates, fostering a high-accountability safety and continuous improvement culture.
Pursue personal professional development through formal and informal Mars learning initiatives while developing training opportunities for team members.
Military Occupational Specialty (MOS) Crosswalk
Your military experience translating complex mission requirements, managing tight schedules, coordinating cargo movements, and leading teams provides directly transferable skills for this role. Candidates with backgrounds in the following service specialties are strongly encouraged to apply:
U.S. Army
MOS 88N (Transportation Management Coordinator): Direct match for freight scheduling, cargo booking, carrier coordination, commercial transport documentation, and movement control system management [source: 1, 6].
MOS 92A (Automated Logistical Specialist - NCO): Excellent alignment with warehouse data management systems, staging, transaction auditing, and supervising inventory operations.
MOS 88M (Motor Transport Operator - Squad Leader / Truck Master): Proven capability managing distribution lines, coordinating vehicle/asset movements, enforcing safety protocols, and leading personnel under shift deadlines.
MOS 92Y (Unit Supply Specialist - NCO / Supply Sergeant): Deep experience with property accountability, vendor coordination, inventory systems, and transactional operations.
Branch 88A / 90A (Transportation / Logistics Officer): Directly translates to leading operational distribution, carrier execution, contract alignment, and cross-functional team supervision.
U.S. Navy
Rating LS / LSS (Logistics Specialist / Logistics Specialist Submarine - Petty Officer): Strong match for inventory data system operations, shipping/receiving supervision, carrier liaison, receipt documentation, and supply chain accountability.

title: Senior Director - Finance Technology Service & Operations Delivery (MF015)
location: USA-Virginia-McLean; USA-Illinois-Chicago
description:
Job Description:
Mars Corporate Finance Technology (FinTech) leads the integrated technology strategy and roadmap for Finance, partnering with our Corporate, Mars Global Services Finance (MGSF), and Segment Finance communities to drive a world-class digital agenda. We shape and deliver these capabilities in partnership with Mars Digital Technologies (DT), and our strategic delivery partners globally. Through an integrated ecosystem of best-in-class Finance platforms, data assets and emerging AI capabilities, FinTech enables strong operational execution of our global financial processes, and accelerated delivery of critical capabilities in support of our global growth aspiration. As a member of the FinTech Senior Leadership Team, the Senior Director - Finance Technology, Service & Operations orchestrates four connected capabilities across our organization: portfolio and program management; service management, including UX and user centricity; financial management; and organizational change effectiveness and adoption. It establishes & leads common governance processes, service and experience standards across FinTech while execution remains distributed across Product Leads, capability teams, DT, MGSF and strategic partners.
Key Responsibilities:
Portfolio and program management: Building a world-class portfolio & program management capability, ensuring consistently reliable delivery of an integrated, multi-year roadmap
Product management and continuous improvement: Establish common product and platform lifecycle standards, outcome measures, backlog disciplines and cross-product ways of working. Product Leads retain accountability for product outcomes, roadmaps and delivery.
Service management and operational governance: Define service standards, controls, SLAs, experience measures and continuous-improvement initiatives for Finance technology services, with particular focus on the financial close, consolidation, reporting/anlaytics and planning cycles.
UX and user centricity: Orchestrate UX and user-centric design as a shared FinTech capability, comparable to the product-management model. Establish common methods for user research, journey mapping, usability testing, accessibility, experience measurement and feedback-to-backlog conversion, while Product Leads and delivery teams apply those methods within their products.
Service management framework & orchestration: Shape and govern clear accountabilities across FinTech, DT, MGSF, Data/MDG teams and strategic partners. Ensure seamless transition from program delivery into sustainable support models ensuring strong ownership & execution by our delivery & service teams
