title: Optical Mechanical Engineer
location: San Francisco
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability.

 - Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management.

 - Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces.

 - Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing.

 - Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access.

 - Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans.

 - Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

 - You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance.

 - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

 - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

 - You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability.

 - You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation.

 - You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements.

Technical Understanding: Support team members with supplier prospecting for your assigned commodity. Develop an understanding of the sourcing process and broader supplier market. Negotiations: Participate in negotiation preparation by providing appropriate data and insight with manager oversight. Understand standard commercial terms applicable to your assigned commodity. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara is seeking a Supply Chain Program Manager (SCPM) to own the supply chain strategy and execution of our new product introductions (NPI) for a portfolio of devices and accessories, from concept through mass production. You will be the connective tissue between Product, Hardware Engineering, Operations, Planning, Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, and Logistics, driving cross-functional alignment on schedule, cost, and supply readiness for complete systems and multiple concurrent programs rather than individual commodities.
You will lead through influence at every level of the organization, up to VP and executive leadership. You'll set the standard for program rhythms across the portfolio, surface risks early, drive decisions across teams and executives with competing priorities, mentor less-senior program managers, and shape Engineering designs that can be built, sourced, and shipped at scale. We also want someone who treats recurring program work (status reporting, risk tracking, readiness checks, data pulls) as something to automate. You'll architect AI agents and workflow automation, and drive their adoption across the team, to free up time for the judgment-heavy work that moves programs forward.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the United States. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.
In this role, you will:
Mastermind and power NPI programs end-to-end
Champion a portfolio of concurrent next-generation device and accessory programs from bold concept stages through EVT, DVT, PVT, explosive ramp, and full mass production, taking full ownership of the end-to-end supply chain master plan and roadmap across programs
Drive flawless launch readiness in close lockstep with world-class JDM partners and internal operations engines, setting multi-program BOM+MVA cost strategy, mastering development E&O, mitigating risk, and executing aggressive ramp curves
Command portfolio-level cost, precision scheduling, and strategic risk, pitching clear, high-impact decisions and trade-offs to VP and executive leadership
Define, evolve, and enforce rigorous build-readiness standards and high-stakes gate reviews at every critical phase—covering materials, custom packaging, and global logistics
Engineer and standardize lead-time-driven backward-scheduling from OK2MP through demanding REL/CRT testing to secure critical PO release deadlines with total precision
Strategically classify process paths early (Full PLCM vs. Legacy Fast-Track exception) and drive ironclad stage-gate documentation from day-one kickoff
Galvanize cross-functional alignment and exert high-impact influence
Serve as the indispensable single point of accountability and catalyst for supply chain excellence across Product, Engineering, Operations, Planning, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, and Marketing
Unify diverse stakeholders around top priorities, resolve friction with agility, and guide VP and executive decisions with compelling options and bold recommendations
Partner dynamically with Hardware Engineering leadership on DFM, design-for-cost, and proactive supply-chain risk mitigation right at the drawing board
Lead high-octane schedule stewardship, synchronizing supply roadmaps directly to the stage-gate timeline and orchestrating high-alignment weekly core-team reviews
Run dynamic program cadences (core team syncs, readiness reviews, executive updates) that catalyze action and drive transformative momentum
Define and standardize seamless, structured handoffs to sustaining Supply Chain Managers post-MP ramp, ensuring long-term operational success and flawless execution
Neutralize supply risks and drive world-class partner performance
Join forces with Sourcing, Planning, and global manufacturing leaders to guarantee resilient supply lines, crush long-lead bottlenecks, and deploy bulletproof contingency strategies
Co-lead Sourcing initiatives with aggressive cost targets, actionable should-cost insights, and high-stakes JDM and supplier negotiations at the leadership level across complex system BOMs
Relentlessly hunt down and resolve capacity, supply, quality, or logistics bottlenecks before they ever threaten the critical path
Own and govern the strategic Materials Risk Buy approval workflow, evaluating financial exposure and securing rapid executive alignment
Manage high-impact engineering changes with precision, driving seamless inventory disposition and cutover plans
Own NPI Material Spend and NMS budgets at the tens-of-millions scale with absolute fiscal rigor across tooling, NRE, and ORT investments
Revolutionize supply chain operations with cutting-edge AI and automation
Architect high-leverage playbooks, intelligent workflows, and custom tooling that supercharge productivity across the entire global supply chain organization
Transform complex data into game-changing insights through futuristic dashboards, predictive risk analytics, and compelling executive briefings
Pioneer autonomous AI agents and automated workflows, and drive their adoption across the org, to handle routine program tasks, status roll-ups, and data pulls, freeing your bandwidth for high-value strategic leadership
Champion emerging AI advancements and translate state-of-the-art tech into transformative, real-world operational advantages
Set data standards for, and maintain, hyper-accurate, modernized supply chain tracking infrastructure across ERP/PLM platforms, PR/PO tracking, and program dashboards
Embody and lead as an inspirational Samsara leader
Embody and champion Samsara's core cultural ethos—Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, and Win as a Team—inspiring everyone around you to achieve extraordinary results, while mentoring and raising the bar for less-senior program managers across the team
Minimum requirements for the role:
10+ years of experience in supply chain program management, NPI, or operations for hardware or electronics products, with a track record of taking multiple products, including flagship launches, from concept to mass production
BS in a relevant field (Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Engineering Management, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain) or equivalent practical experience
Demonstrated ability to lead multiple complex, cross-functional programs concurrently and influence VP and executive stakeholders without direct authority
Deep expertise in the NPI lifecycle and builds (EVT, DVT, PVT), BOM and ECO management, and CM and JDM operations
Experience leading relationships with international manufacturing and supply partners at executive levels, including commercial negotiations and cost-down agreements
Advanced analytical skills, with the ability to turn data into insights and craft clear executive presentations
Strong organizational skills: prioritization across a portfolio of programs, attention to detail, and triage of complicated issues
Self-motivated, proactive problem solver who is comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous settings
Hands-on experience architecting and deploying AI tools, agents, or automation (for example LLM-based workflows, scripting, or low-code tools) to streamline recurring work, and driving adoption beyond your own team
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience with IoT, telematics, or connected hardware, including accessories, cables, and sensors
Experience with ERP, PLM, and planning systems (for example NetSuite) and SQL or Python for data analysis
Experience building internal tools or agents that other team members adopt, and mentoring less-senior program managers
PMP or equivalent program management certification

title: Head of Global Partnerships and Startup and Ecosystem Product, Finance & Strategy
location: SF, NYC, SEA
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Our team partners with Stripe’s Chief Business Officer and leaders across Global Partnerships and Startup and Ecosystem Product. Global Partnerships builds and manages relationships with banks, networks, payment methods, and other strategic partners that enable Stripe’s products and global expansion. The Startup and Ecosystem Product teams build tools and capabilities that help founders start and grow businesses and partners to extend Stripe products to better serve users across our entire ecosystem, respectively.
The Finance & Strategy team brings financial rigor, strategic clarity, and analytical depth to the decisions that shape Stripe’s business and long-term growth strategy. We act as a strategic finance function for complex commercial partner negotiations and work with product leaders to shape their strategy, growth, investment priorities, and financial performance as it scales. We help leaders evaluate partner economics, allocate resources, establish goals, and understand performance in order to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations.
What you’ll do
We’re looking for a finance leader to lead Finance & Strategy for Global Partnerships and Startup and Ecosystem Product. You’ll serve as a trusted financial and strategic advisor to the Chief Business Officer and other senior business leaders, connecting commercial decisions to their financial implications.
You’ll lead a team of strategic finance professionals to craft deal analysis and structure recommendations, investment frameworks, and strategic insights that drive long-term economic growth for Stripe. In addition, you will work cross-functionally to ensure disciplined financial planning and forecasting. You’ll develop the team, establish clear priorities, and balance time-sensitive deal support with recurring financial commitments and targeted strategic analysis.
Responsibilities
Lead the financial evaluation of complex product enablement partnerships. Partner with Global Partnerships leaders and Partner Development Managers to evaluate and execute commercial agreements with new and existing partners, bringing an independent financial perspective to negotiation strategy and decisions.
Guide deal economics and investment analysis. Oversee financial modeling, commercial benchmarking, scenario analysis, and investment cases. Translate complex deal structures into clear assessments of financial impact, risks, returns, and commercial trade-offs.
Improve partner economics and performance visibility. Develop data-driven insights to identify strategic and optimization opportunities for Stripe’s partner portfolio. Establish consistent frameworks and metrics to assess partner initiatives and deals.
Build investment cases in support of new business initiatives. Craft financial models in support of Startup and Ecosystem Product initiatives and establish objectives and metrics in partnership with Business and Product leaders.
Actively contribute to org building as part of the F&S leadership team. Help shape and execute F&S priorities, influence and drive cross-functional initiatives, and contribute to culture building of the organization.
Coordinate cross-functional financial recommendations. Work closely with Product and Engineering, Pricing, Strategy and Operations, Treasury Finance, Accounting, and other Finance & Strategy teams to support planning and forecasting activities.
Own the financial planning and forecasting cycle. Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and business reviews for Global Partnerships and Startup and Ecosystem Product areas.
Guide operating expense management. Maintain visibility into resource plans, assess investment and efficiency trade-offs, and surface material changes that require leadership decisions.
Partner on goals, metrics, and performance. Help leaders establish financial objectives and key business metrics for priority businesses and initiatives. Explain material deviations from plan, identify underlying drivers, and recommend actions.
Build and develop a high-performing team. Coach and develop direct reports, set clear expectations, and maintain high standards for analytical quality, business partnership, and execution.
Scale the team’s effectiveness. Improve financial models, reporting, planning processes, and analytical infrastructure. Use AI, automation, and better tooling to reduce manual work and create capacity for higher-value analysis.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
15+ years in strategic finance, commercial finance, product finance, or FP&A, with demonstrated success leading and developing finance teams.
Strong commercial judgment and experience evaluating complex partnership agreements, building investment cases, and supporting negotiations through rigorous financial analysis.
Strong grounding in budgeting, forecasting, headcount and operating expense planning, and business performance management.
A proven ability to build trusted relationships with executives and cross-functional leaders, provide an objective perspective, and influence consequential decisions.
Exceptional analytical and financial modeling capabilities, with the ability to connect detailed economics to broader business strategy.
A hands-on leadership style and the judgment to prioritize across urgent transactions, recurring operating commitments, and longer-term strategic work.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting complex financial information and recommendations to senior leaders.
Comfort working with large, complex datasets, a working knowledge of SQL, and the ability to create structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.
Preferred qualifications
Experience at a high-growth payments company, fintech, or bank
Deep understanding of payments unit economics, including card networks, banks, and the role of partnerships in enabling financial products.
Prior experience in investment banking, private equity, or another transaction-oriented analytical role.
Experience using AI, automation, and financial planning or analytics tools to improve the quality and scalability of finance work.

title: Indirect Tax Systems Specialst
location: Seattle, San Francisco, Chicago, New York, Remote
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
What You’ll Do
As technology evolves, so do our tax reporting requirements, especially with the multitude of state and local taxes around the US.  Our state-related indirect obligations and filing requirements continue to grow with the business, and we are looking for someone who can not only maintain but help further build our US sales tax practice in achieving our tax goals.  This individual will need to be versed in indirect tax systems used in compliance, and be able to work with our talented group of engineers who support the state tax function. This position will report to the State & Local Tax Lead.
This position can be office-based in Seattle, South San Francisco, Chicago, New York City, or Remote-US.
Responsibilities
Help establish the direction, goals, and priorities for Stripe’s US indirect tax function, with a strong moral compass and integrity.
Manage and improve state indirect tax compliance systems across our portfolio of companies, and work with the tax reporting and eng teams to ensure coverage on all of our tax filings.  This includes systems used in compliance filings, business registrations, and working with our both tax and non-tax vendors to ensure we are meeting our compliance obligations.
Oversee and run point on special projects impacting US indirect tax systems.
Run models and analyses for state indirect tax planning.
Assist in data collection used in state controversy across different tax types and resolve tax issues.
Monitor SALT developments across the US, including local impacts of federal law.
Proactively identify areas for operational improvements and implement solutions to streamline downstream US indirect tax reporting.
Participate in special projects as needed including state tax attribute studies, nexus reviews, and evaluating state tax impacts of new tax regimes, M&A transactions, and new products before they launch.
Who You Are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum Requirements
6+ years of relevant indirect tax experience, including in public accounting (Big 4 preferred) and/or - preferably - at a multinational publicly listed company.
Deep knowledge of state indirect tax issues and solutions in the technology industry.
A strong background in tax compliance, specifically US indirect taxes.
Experience in working with teams and engineers in building out US indirect tax infrastructure.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to research and communicate complex technical tax issues clearly to non-tax team members and work effectively across functional teams.
Flexibility to react quickly to changes in state tax laws including proposed changes as well as changes in the company’s products and services.
Exhibit strong analytical thinking, ability to work in a fast-paced environment with excellent prioritization and organizational skills.
Empathy, humility, and some comedy
You will also likely have (not required):
An advanced degree or professional qualification in tax, accounting, or law (CPA, JD or Master’s degree).
Experience working in a high-growth, rapidly scaling environment.
Industry experience at a multinational organization; experience working in technology, payments, or financial services is a plus.
A willingness to work with a diverse crew of tax nerds who care deeply about Stripe’s tax issues and each other.

The Proactive Threat team finds vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across Stripe's systems, applications, networks, and cloud infrastructure before adversaries do. We run penetration tests, emulate real-world threat actors in red team operations, and work closely with our defensive security teams to validate detection capabilities and improve Stripe's overall security posture.
We are builders first. We build custom tooling, automation frameworks, and internal platforms that scale our offensive work and make our assessments repeatable and high-fidelity. Increasingly, that includes AI agents that find and validate vulnerabilities at a scale no human team could reach. We believe the best offensive security engineers are equal parts hacker and engineer.
The team is distributed and works regularly with security, engineering, and product stakeholders across Stripe, including teams in Europe and Asia.
What you'll do
As a Staff Offensive Security Engineer on the Proactive Threat team, you'll set the technical direction for how Stripe tests itself the way a real adversary would. You'll be the team's most senior offensive practitioner. You'll stay deeply hands-on: you'll lead the hardest engagements yourself and write the tooling that makes everyone around you more effective.
You'll own the strategy and the operating foundation of our red team program, including its tradecraft, infrastructure, rules of engagement, and coordination with detection and response. You'll shape how offensive security scales at Stripe through automation and agentic systems. Your work will span multiple teams: you'll partner with detection engineering, incident response, vulnerability management, and product engineering so that what we find makes Stripe measurably harder to attack.

Technical strategy and leadership
Set the multi-quarter technical strategy for offensive security at Stripe: where we test, how deep we go, and which threat actors and attack paths matter most to a financial infrastructure company
Define and own the red team program's operating foundation: rules of engagement, opsec standards, C2 and payload infrastructure, IR deconfliction, and repeatable engagement playbooks
Be the prime mover on large, ambiguous offensive initiatives that span multiple teams, from framing the problem to landing the outcome
Make fast, well-reasoned calls on scope, risk, and tradecraft, and explain them clearly to engineers, security leaders, and executives

Lead the team's most complex engagements yourself: objective-based red team operations, assumed-breach exercises, and deep assessments of critical payment, money-movement, cloud, CI/CD, and corporate systems

Find novel vulnerability classes and attack chains specific to Stripe's architecture, and turn them into systemic fixes rather than one-off findings
Scaling through engineering and automation
Design and build the offensive platforms, tooling, and agentic workflows that encode the team's expertise into repeatable, scalable systems
Apply LLMs and autonomous agents to reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploit validation, and reporting, and set the bar for running them safely and reliably

The role

We're looking for a Portfolio Manager in the San Francisco Bay Area to join our Commercial Operations team. You'll manage revenue performance for a portfolio of battery storage assets that Tyba operates in wholesale power markets.

Each asset has a main performance target (for example, day-ahead TBx capture). You'll track how each asset does against its target, figure out why it's over- or underperforming, and work with customers and internal teams to improve it. You'll be the main point of contact for your customers and will work closely with our Market Operations, Market Analytics, Modeling, Sales, and Product teams.

   - Review each asset's revenue and dispatch daily to catch recurring problems.
   
   - When an asset misses its target or cycles more or less than planned, analyze prices and dispatch to find out why, then get it fixed.
   
   - Work with Modeling and Market Analytics to improve performance. Report suspected model or forecast issues with supporting data, prioritize them by revenue impact, and use market insights to shape each customer's strategy.

 - Manage each customer's operating strategy.
   
   - Agree with the customer on each asset's operating strategy, including the performance target, baseline, operating limits, plans for high-value days, and when we can make manual changes.
   
   - Advise customers on specific needs such as warranty cycle limits, hedges, and congestion.

 - Manage the customer relationship.
   
   - Be the main point of contact for your accounts. Run biweekly performance meetings and quarterly executive business reviews (EBRs) on how assets are performing, what we're improving, and why.
   
   - Track account health and churn risk, own renewals, and share customer feedback and product gaps with Product and Engineering.

 - Lead implementations and find growth.
   
   - Lead onboarding for new customers and new assets from sales handoff to go-live, including account planning and complex asset and market integrations.
   
   - Spot expansion opportunities through your performance work and customers' goals, and pass them to the Account Executive.

 - Bachelor's degree (or foreign equivalent) in Economics, Finance, Engineering, or another quantitative field.
